newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-THORPE CENTURY SHUTS NZ OUT OF 1ST TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-THORPE CENTURY SHUTS NZ OUT OF 1ST TEST.

text.p: A majestic century by England's Graham Thorpe and composed play from Dominic Cork shut New Zealand out of the first cricket test on the fourth morning at Eden Park on Monday.

The pair batted throughout the morning session to take England from their overnight 366 for six to 448 for six, with Thorpe posting his third test hundred and Cork closing in on his second half-century.
Thorpe was on 117 and Cork had reached 38 at the interval.
New Zealand's hopes of knocking England's last four wickets over in the morning session dissipated as Thorpe and Cork took full advantage of mediocre bowling on a pitch still playing easily.

Thorpe, who started the day on 57, moved swiftly to his hundred after finding his bearings in the first hour. He took four boundaries in the space of two wayward Danny Morrison overs to get his century, which came off 211 balls in just under five hours and included 15 fours.
It was the third century of the test, after New Zealander Stephen Fleming's 129 and Alec Stewart's 173 earlier in the England innings.
Fast-medium bowler Cork curbed his natural aggression to demonstrate considerable skill with the bat and was untroubled by the New Zealand bowlers.

Their century stand came up in 221 balls and at lunch Thorpe and Cork were closing in on the English seventh wicket record of 149 against New Zealand. That mark was established on Eden Park in 1970-71 by Alan Knott and Peter Lever.
The only New Zealand bowler able to keep the batsmen watchful this morning was offspinner Dipak Patel, whose seven-over spell cost only 11 runs.
